title: Aspects of Madness
subtitle: Dreams are the first and last dance partner of madness.

trails.title: A Journey to and Fro
trails.description: There is a passage here, its author unknown.

content.text:
I return once more to Comala Prison. To me, this massive cage is no longer an inescapable labyrinth. When I left, the lady from Manus Vindictae did not stop me, yet I could still feel her gaze—so sorrowful, so blurred, so cold—never once shifting away from me.

On the streets of Ushuaia, a young girl pointed me back toward the prison. That severed thread tugged at my heart, and I knew with certainty that my mission lay here. If I were placed before "fate," my life and death would seemingly follow a predetermined path to its destined end. And as I walk this path, I must carry not even a shred of hesitation.

It is time to speak with "Aleph," the one who answers all questions.

items.text: Aspects of Madness

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: "Dear Urd,"

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: "Why are you so interested in the Panopticon of Comala?"

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: "Dear Mr. Aleph,"

items.speaker: Dores
items.text: Whether as a doctor or a writer, I simply cannot turn a blind eye to the friction around me, especially the discord and injustice I've witnessed here in Comala.

items.speaker: Dores
items.text: So, I would ask of you a question: Is there any way to resolve the endless conflicts in this place?

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: To put an end to this, a true ending is required.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: Your arrival has made it possible for this simulation to have an ending—or rather, a victory.

items.speaker: Dores
items.text: What do you mean by "victory"? I'd appreciate it if you could clarify in simple terms. If this victory comes at the cost of any inmate's life, I'm afraid I cannot accept it.

items.speaker: Dores
items.text: I also have another question for you: If I leave, will the stories and conflicts here come to an end?

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: Ms. Grace of Manus Vindictae will grant you passage. But in any case, the cycle of history will continue to repeat itself in this prison, and in the entire world.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: The sins of humankind will not cease until veins turn to wires, flesh and bone to geometric shapes, and the world around us twists in the colors of an oil painting.

items.speaker: Dores
items.text: I must say, your words have left me rather baffled. Fragments of the events you describe often appear in my dreams. Could it be that these things really happened?

items.speaker: Dores
items.text: If that's the case, why can't I recall the details? Why am I left with only disconnected pieces?

items.speaker: Dores
items.text: The madness in Comala, these bizarre dreams ... I must put an end to them.

items.speaker: Dores
items.text: What have I forgotten? Has someone or something altered my memory? I can't shake the feeling that something crucial to me has been lost in the river of time. Some kind of duty, perhaps.

items.speaker: Dores
items.text: What should I do? How can I recapture what I've lost?

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: I won't answer a question that already has an answer, one given to you by the person who escorted you here and made you a promise.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: You're so close to the place where the truth lies. Think carefully. Why are you here?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: These letters we found have answered a great deal, but there's still something that isn't clear.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Mr. Aleph, what exactly did the Manus promise Dr. Dores?

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: An era. A chance for her to remember her duty.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: An era?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You helped her leave the Panopticon in the end. Where did she go?
Momentarily roused from his dream, the prisoner looks blankly for a moment before his gaze drifts back toward the distant illusion.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: Southward.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: There, on the no-man's continent, Manus Vindictae is preparing to recreate the parable of the past and future.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: A glorious past and a glimmering future belonging to arcanists.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: Dr. Dores is deeply connected to this particular parable.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Hmm. What exactly are the Manus planning to do in Antarctica?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: And why would Dr. Dores go there voluntarily?
The information revealed stirs unease in the hearts of the investigators from the Foundation.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Mr. Aleph, when did Dr. Dores depart?

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: It was a day when both the clouds and sun were visible.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: A day when both the clouds and sun were visible? Could you be more specific?

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: Specific? You mean the time of day?
His mind long ago lost any sense of time, a necessary exchange to make room for an infinite cosmos of words.
He once again finds himself without an answer.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: When both clouds and the sun were visible? Hey, Vertin, I think I know!

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: It was three days ago! Then, Dr. Dores wasn't going to Comala on the day I met her.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: She was leaving. She was headed to Antarctica!

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: It was cloudy that afternoon, with a brief spell of sunshine, just like Aleph described.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Then it hasn't been long since she left. Excellent news.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Three days. If we set off immediately, we might still catch up to her.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: But based on the intel we gathered in Ushuaia, Manus Vindictae bombed the entire port three days ago.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Clearly, they wanted to prevent any interference from the Foundation. It's unlikely we'll find any functioning ships there.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I'll report the situation to the Buenos Aires branch. Timekeeper, I'm afraid we'll have to find another way to get there.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: I have a boat.
A small boat gifted by Manus Vindictae.
During the past several "Storms," he has taken this boat, traveling to Antarctica at Manus Vindictae's invitation to evade the reversion.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Could you lend it to us? The situation's urgent, Mr. Aleph.
Secret Dock, Ushuaia
Beneath a decrypted lighthouse, a battered little boat bobs in sync with the waves.
It is small and fragile, not the kind that seems capable of braving an icy sea.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: This boat will automatically take you to McMurdo Port, the landing point Manus Vindictae established by the shores of the Ross Sea.
Sonetto eyes the boat with skepticism, rightfully distrusting this "advisor" of Manus Vindictae.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: This looks like Manus technology. Its arcane energy source is highly unstable.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper, I suggest we wait for support in Ushuaia.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: I don't usually agree with Sonetto, but I have to admit, I don't have much confidence that a boat this small can actually make it to Antarctica.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Mr. Aleph, do you know anything about Manus Vindictae's ritual? How far has it progressed?

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: The ritual could begin at any moment. I believe that's why they left Comala.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: Upon departure, one of their members, a woman named Grace, told me they would seal off the sea.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Are we too late?

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: If you wish to find Dores, you must follow the same path she took.
The distant drone of the raging waves fills their background like a repeating omen.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I see. Mr. Aleph, members of the Foundation branch will arrive soon to evaluate your condition. I hope you'll answer their questions with the same patience you showed us. Thank you.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Sonetto, let's go.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Yes, Timekeeper.
As always, Sonetto keeps any mission-irrelevant queries to herself.
The girls preparing to set sail turn to the young writer beside them.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Thank you for your assistance too, Recoleta. Perhaps you'll consider joining the—
A thunderous crash echoes from behind them—the sound of a collapsing building.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: What was that? It came from the Panopticon!
